name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs gently poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce — perfect with warm bread.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and pepper and cook for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt, then simmer for 8–10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Make 6 small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with chopped parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread.
tips: Add crumbled feta in the last two minutes for extra richness.
photo: Eggs gently poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce — perfect with warm bread.

name: Ful Medames
description: Egypt’s beloved breakfast of warm fava beans with garlic, lemon, cumin and olive oil.
steps: Tip the beans with their liquid into a pan and warm over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Mash about half the beans with a fork or potato masher.
Stir in the crushed garlic, cumin, lemon juice and salt.
Spoon into bowls, drizzle generously with olive oil and top with diced tomato and parsley.
Serve with warm pita bread.
tips: A boiled egg and some sliced cucumber make this a complete breakfast.
photo: Egypt’s beloved breakfast of warm fava beans with garlic, lemon, cumin and olive oil.

name: Menemen
description: Soft Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and green peppers.
steps: Melt the butter with the oil in a frying pan. Add the chopped peppers and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the grated or finely chopped tomatoes and cook until most of the liquid has gone, about 6 minutes.
Season with salt and chili flakes.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently until just set but still soft.
Serve immediately with fresh bread.
tips: Take it off the heat while it still looks slightly wet — it keeps cooking.
photo: Soft Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and green peppers.

name: Za'atar Manakish
description: Soft Lebanese flatbreads topped with za’atar and olive oil, baked until golden.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add the warm water and 2 tablespoons of the oil and knead for 8 minutes into a soft dough.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oven to 240°C (465°F) with a tray inside.
Mix the za’atar with the remaining olive oil to a loose paste.
Divide the dough into 6, roll each into a thin round and press dimples into the surface with your fingertips.
Spread with the za’atar oil and bake for 6–8 minutes until the edges are golden.
tips: Serve with labneh, cucumber, tomato and fresh mint.
photo: Soft Lebanese flatbreads topped with za’atar and olive oil, baked until golden.

name: Date & Tahini Overnight Oats
description: Creamy no-cook oats sweetened with dates — ideal for suhoor.
steps: Chop the dates finely, removing the stones.
Stir together the oats, milk, yogurt, dates and cinnamon in a jar or bowl.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
In the morning, stir well and drizzle with tahini before eating.
tips: Slow-release oats and dates keep you full through a long fast.
photo: Creamy no-cook oats sweetened with dates — ideal for suhoor.

name: Lentil Soup (Shorbat Adas)
description: A silky red lentil soup with cumin and lemon — a Ramadan table favourite.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the chopped onion and carrot for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until the lentils are very soft.
Blend until smooth, then season with salt.
Serve with lemon wedges and toasted pita.
tips: Freezes well for up to 3 months — make a double batch before Ramadan.
photo: A silky red lentil soup with cumin and lemon — a Ramadan table favourite.

name: Chicken Shawarma Wraps
description: Spiced, juicy chicken wrapped with garlic sauce and pickles.
steps: Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, 2 crushed garlic cloves, spices, oil and a pinch of salt. Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 15 minutes (or overnight).
Cook the chicken in a hot pan or under the grill for 6–7 minutes a side until cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Stir the remaining crushed garlic into a little yogurt with salt for a quick garlic sauce.
Fill warm pitas with chicken, sauce, pickles and sliced tomato, then roll up tightly.
tips: Toast the rolled wraps in a dry pan for a crisp outside.
photo: Spiced, juicy chicken wrapped with garlic sauce and pickles.

name: Fattoush Salad
description: Crunchy Lebanese salad with toasted pita and a tangy sumac dressing.
steps: Tear the pita into pieces and toast in a hot oven or dry pan until crisp.
Chop the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes and radishes and place in a large bowl with the herbs.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, pomegranate molasses and a pinch of salt.
Toss the salad with the dressing and pita just before serving.
tips: Add the pita at the last moment so it stays crunchy.
photo: Crunchy Lebanese salad with toasted pita and a tangy sumac dressing.

name: Falafel with Tahini Sauce
description: Crisp herby falafel made from soaked chickpeas, with a lemony tahini sauce.
steps: Soak the dried chickpeas in plenty of cold water for 12–24 hours, then drain well (do not use canned).
Blitz the chickpeas, onion, garlic, herbs, cumin and salt in a food processor to a coarse paste. Stir in the baking soda.
Shape into small patties or balls.
Heat the oil to 175°C (350°F) and fry in batches for 3–4 minutes until deep golden. Drain on paper.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice, a pinch of salt and enough cold water to make a pourable sauce.
Serve the falafel in pita or on a plate with salad and the tahini sauce.
tips: If the mixture won’t hold, chill it for 30 minutes before shaping.
photo: Crisp herby falafel made from soaked chickpeas, with a lemony tahini sauce.

name: Chicken Biryani
description: Fragrant layered rice and spiced chicken — a celebration dish for Eid and family gatherings.
steps: Soak the rice for 30 minutes. Warm the milk and soak the saffron in it.
Fry the thinly sliced onions in the oil until deep golden. Remove half for garnish.

Add the ginger garlic paste and chicken to the pan and cook for 5 minutes. Add tomatoes, yogurt, biryani masala, green chilies and salt and cook covered for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce thick.
Meanwhile, boil the rice in well-salted water for 5–6 minutes until 70% cooked, then drain.
Layer half the rice over the chicken, scatter with mint, coriander and fried onions, then add the remaining rice. Drizzle with the saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes (dum) until the rice is fluffy.
Gently mix the layers as you serve.
tips: Seal the lid with foil for the dum step so the steam stays in.
photo: Fragrant layered rice and spiced chicken — a celebration dish for Eid and family gatherings.

name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Olives and Lemon
description: Slow-cooked chicken with preserved lemon, green olives, ginger and saffron.
steps: Rub the chicken with the spices, crushed garlic, a pinch of salt and 1 tablespoon of oil.
Heat the remaining oil in a tagine or heavy pot and brown the chicken on both sides. Remove.
Soften the sliced onions for 8 minutes, then return the chicken with the stock and saffron.
Cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes.
Add the sliced preserved lemon rind and olives and cook uncovered for 10 more minutes to reduce the sauce.
Scatter with coriander and serve with bread or couscous.
tips: No preserved lemon? Use the zest of one lemon plus a squeeze of juice at the end.
photo: Slow-cooked chicken with preserved lemon, green olives, ginger and saffron.

name: Lamb Kofta with Yogurt Sauce
description: Grilled spiced lamb skewers with a cool garlic and mint yogurt.
steps: Grate the onion and squeeze out the excess juice.
Mix the lamb, onion, 2 crushed garlic cloves, chopped parsley, spices and salt. Knead for 2 minutes.
Shape into 12 sausage shapes around skewers and chill for 10 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry for 10–12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Stir the remaining garlic and chopped mint into the yogurt with a pinch of salt.
Serve the kofta with the yogurt, salad and rice or flatbread.
tips: Wet your hands while shaping so the mixture doesn’t stick.
photo: Grilled spiced lamb skewers with a cool garlic and mint yogurt.

name: Chicken Karahi
description: A rich, tomato-based Pakistani curry cooked fast in a wok-like karahi.
steps: Heat the oil in a karahi or wide pan and fry the chicken on high heat for 5 minutes.
Add the crushed garlic and half the grated ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, salt, chili powder and ground coriander. Cover and cook for 15 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
Uncover and cook on high, stirring, until the oil separates from the sauce.
Add the green chilies, remaining ginger (in thin strips) and garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes.
Garnish with coriander and serve with naan or rice.
tips: Peel the tomatoes for a smoother sauce.
photo: A rich, tomato-based Pakistani curry cooked fast in a wok-like karahi.

name: Daal Tadka
description: Comforting yellow lentils finished with a sizzling spiced ghee tempering.
steps: Rinse the lentils and simmer with 3 cups of water, the turmeric and salt for 25 minutes until soft.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and add the cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add the sliced garlic, chopped onion and chili and fry until golden.
Add the chopped tomato and garam masala and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the lentils, stir and garnish with coriander.
tips: Serve with basmati rice or roti and a squeeze of lemon.
photo: Comforting yellow lentils finished with a sizzling spiced ghee tempering.

name: Nasi Lemak
description: Malaysia’s national dish: fragrant coconut rice with sambal, egg, cucumber and peanuts.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with the coconut milk, 1 cup of water, a pinch of salt and the knotted pandan leaves.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, then cool and halve.
For the sambal, fry the sliced onion in oil until soft, add the chili paste and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the tamarind, sugar and a splash of water and simmer until thick.
Fry the anchovies until crisp (or skip for a lighter version).
Serve the rice with sambal, egg, cucumber slices, peanuts and anchovies.
tips: Fried chicken (ayam goreng) turns this into a feast.
photo: Malaysia’s national dish: fragrant coconut rice with sambal, egg, cucumber and peanuts.

name: Beef Rendang
description: Slow-cooked dry beef curry in coconut and spices — rich, tender and deeply flavoured.
steps: Soak the dried chilies, then blend with the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal and turmeric into a paste.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan until golden, then pound or blend until oily.
Fry the spice paste in the oil for 8 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef cubes, bruised lemongrass and lime leaves and stir to coat.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered on low for 2½–3 hours, stirring often, until the sauce has almost completely reduced.
Stir in the toasted coconut, palm sugar and salt and cook until dark and dry.
tips: Rendang tastes even better the next day.
photo: Slow-cooked dry beef curry in coconut and spices — rich, tender and deeply flavoured.

name: Jollof Rice with Chicken
description: Smoky, tomatoey West African rice served with seasoned chicken.
steps: Season the chicken with curry powder, thyme and salt, then roast at 200°C (400°F) for 35 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, peppers, scotch bonnet and one onion until smooth.
Fry the other sliced onion in the oil, add the tomato paste and fry for 3 minutes, then add the blended mixture and cook for 15 minutes until reduced.
Add the washed rice, stock and bay leaves. Stir once, cover tightly and cook on low for 25–30 minutes.
Fluff the rice and serve with the roast chicken.
tips: Letting the bottom catch slightly gives the prized smoky ‘party jollof’ flavour.
photo: Smoky, tomatoey West African rice served with seasoned chicken.

name: Somali Chicken Suqaar
description: Quick-fried chicken pieces with vegetables and Somali xawaash spice.
steps: Cut the chicken into small cubes and season with xawaash and salt.
Fry the chicken in hot oil for 6–8 minutes until browned.
Add the onion, garlic, diced carrot and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato and cook until the vegetables are just tender.
Finish with coriander and lime juice. Serve with rice, pasta or flatbread.
tips: Xawaash is a blend of cumin, coriander, black pepper, cardamom, cinnamon and turmeric.
photo: Quick-fried chicken pieces with vegetables and Somali xawaash spice.

name: Mujaddara
description: Humble lentils and rice crowned with sweet, crispy onions.
steps: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Slowly fry the thinly sliced onions in the oil for 25–30 minutes until deep brown and crisp. Remove half for topping.
Add the rice and cumin to the pan with the remaining onions and stir for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, salt and 2 cups of water. Cover and simmer for 18 minutes until the rice is cooked.
Serve topped with crispy onions and a spoonful of yogurt.
tips: A simple tomato-cucumber salad is the classic side.
photo: Humble lentils and rice crowned with sweet, crispy onions.

name: Maqluba
description: The ‘upside-down’ pot of spiced rice, chicken and fried vegetables, flipped at the table.
steps: Boil the chicken with the halved onion, cinnamon stick, bay leaves and salt for 40 minutes. Keep the broth.
Soak the rice for 30 minutes, then drain and season with baharat and turmeric.
Slice the eggplant and potatoes and break the cauliflower into florets. Fry (or roast with oil) until golden.
Layer in a large pot: chicken pieces, then the fried vegetables, then the rice.
Pour over enough hot broth to cover the rice by 2 cm. Cover and cook on low for 30–35 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, place a large tray on top and flip the pot in one confident move. Top with toasted almonds.
tips: Tap the bottom of the pot before lifting to help it release cleanly.
photo: The ‘upside-down’ pot of spiced rice, chicken and fried vegetables, flipped at the table.

name: Harira
description: Morocco’s hearty tomato, lentil and chickpea soup traditionally served to break the fast.
steps: Brown the diced lamb in a large pot with a little oil, then add the chopped onion, celery and spices.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, lentils, half the chopped herbs and 2 litres of water. Simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the drained chickpeas and vermicelli and cook for 10 minutes.
Whisk the flour with a cup of cold water and stir it in slowly, simmering for 5 minutes until silky.
Stir in the remaining herbs and serve with lemon wedges and dates.
tips: Serve with dates and chebakia for a classic Moroccan iftar.
photo: Morocco’s hearty tomato, lentil and chickpea soup traditionally served to break the fast.

name: Classic Hummus
description: Ultra-smooth chickpea dip with tahini, lemon and garlic.
steps: Drain the chickpeas (for extra smoothness, simmer them for 10 minutes and slip off the skins).
Blend the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt until thick and pale.
Add the chickpeas and blend, pouring in the ice water a little at a time, for 3–4 minutes until very smooth.
Spread in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and dust with paprika.
tips: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.
photo: Ultra-smooth chickpea dip with tahini, lemon and garlic.

name: Date & Nut Energy Balls
description: No-bake bites of dates, nuts and coconut — great for lunchboxes and iftar.
steps: Pit the dates. If they are firm, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Pulse the nuts in a food processor until finely chopped.
Add the dates, cocoa and cinnamon and blend until the mixture sticks together.
Roll into 16 balls and coat in coconut. Chill for 30 minutes.
tips: Store in the fridge for up to a week.
photo: No-bake bites of dates, nuts and coconut — great for lunchboxes and iftar.

name: Basbousa
description: Golden semolina cake soaked in fragrant syrup — an Eid favourite.
steps: Make the syrup: boil 1 cup of the sugar with the water for 8 minutes, add a squeeze of lemon and the rose water, then cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a 23 × 33 cm tin.
Mix the semolina, remaining sugar, coconut, baking powder, melted butter and yogurt into a thick batter.
Spread in the tin, score into diamonds and press an almond into each.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden, then pour the cool syrup over the hot cake.
Let it absorb the syrup for at least 1 hour before cutting.
tips: Hot cake + cool syrup is the secret to a moist basbousa.
photo: Golden semolina cake soaked in fragrant syrup — an Eid favourite.

name: Kheer (Rice Pudding)
description: Creamy slow-cooked rice pudding with cardamom, pistachios and almonds.
steps: Rinse and soak the rice for 20 minutes, then crush it lightly with your fingers.
Bring the milk to the boil with the crushed cardamom, add the rice and simmer on low for 40 minutes, stirring often.
When thick and creamy, stir in the sugar and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the rose water, then serve warm or chilled, topped with chopped nuts.
tips: Stir the bottom of the pan regularly so the milk doesn’t catch.
photo: Creamy slow-cooked rice pudding with cardamom, pistachios and almonds.

name: Lemon Herb Baked Salmon
description: A quick weeknight salmon with garlic, lemon and fresh herbs.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a tray with parchment.
Place the salmon on the tray and season with salt and pepper.
Mix the oil, crushed garlic, lemon zest and juice and spoon over the fish.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the salmon flakes easily.
Scatter with chopped dill and serve with rice or roasted vegetables.
tips: Thicker fillets may need 2–3 more minutes.
photo: A quick weeknight salmon with garlic, lemon and fresh herbs.

name: Chicken Kabsa
description: Saudi Arabia’s fragrant spiced rice with chicken, raisins and almonds.
steps: Soak the rice for 30 minutes.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil until golden, add the garlic, kabsa spice and chicken pieces and brown for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, pierced dried limes, grated carrot and 5 cups of water. Simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Remove the chicken and roast it in a hot oven for 10 minutes to crisp the skin.
Add the drained rice to the broth (topping up to cover by 1 cm), cover and cook on low for 20 minutes.
Serve the rice on a large platter topped with the chicken, raisins and almonds.
tips: Serve with a simple tomato salsa (daqoos) on the side.
photo: Saudi Arabia’s fragrant spiced rice with chicken, raisins and almonds.
